Praga-Południe — Warsaw, Poland

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

South of Praga-Północ across the Skaryszewski park: mostly post-war residential, with the National Stadium at its river edge. It records the second-highest crime count of Warsaw's districts — 2,160 in the year to June 2024 in the figures reported locally — on a large population, and the reporting describes the usual property crime rather than anything targeted. Few visitors stay here.

Frequently asked questions

Is Praga-Południe safe?

Wandroz currently rates Praga-Południe in Warsaw as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Warsaw during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Warsaw at night. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Warsaw publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Praga-Południe safe at night?

At night, Praga-Południe is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Warsaw. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Praga-Południe a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Praga-Południe's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Warsaw) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
